dedupe_keys.name: pctran desktop nuclear power plant simulator micro simulation technology

description: PCTRAN is a desktop simulator for light water nuclear reactors made by Micro-Simulation Technology since 1985. The home page read on 2026-09-26 lists models for PWR, BWR, the EPR, AP1000, ABWR and ESBWR, a severe accident scope for BWR5, and RadPuff for dose dispersion; it says the IAEA has used PCTRAN as the training platform of its annual simulators workshop, and names licensees including the Military Institute of Science and Technology of Bangladesh (VVER-1200) and Korean nuclear bodies (APR1400, OPR1000 and SMART). Coverage is plant types, not countries, with plant-specific models installed at utilities and institutions for training, analysis, probabilistic safety assessment and emergency exercises. Access is by licence from the company; free download modules exist but, as the page says, the demonstration versions have a runtime limit. Caveats: the page mixes product facts with promotional claims about AI-based accident prevention that were not checked, and model details are not published openly. Simulation uses are accident and emergency response exercises, cascading failure sequences in plant systems, including cyber attack drills described on the page, and generation of accident data for machine learning. Related records: data-nppad-nuclear-power-plant-accident-data is an open simulated accident data set, and model-flexpart-lagrangian-dispersion models atmospheric releases.
